meta.notes: Obligations corpus expanded toward 35 rows (software-only high-risk path). Schema v2 + applies_if.

obligations.title: Risk Management System
obligations.description: Establish, document, implement, maintain and update a risk management system in relation to high-risk AI systems.
obligations.guidance: Document risk assessment methodology, identified risks and mitigation measures. Regular reviews required.

obligations.title: Data Governance and Quality Management
obligations.description: Training, validation and testing data sets shall be subject to data governance and management practices covering design choices, collection processes, preparation operations, assumptions, assessment of availability, quantity and suitability, examination for bias, and identification of gaps. Data sets shall be relevant, sufficiently representative, and to the best extent possible free of errors and complete.
obligations.guidance: Document design choices, collection processes, preparation operations, assumptions, availability/quantity/suitability assessments, bias examination, and identified gaps. Ensure training, validation and testing data sets are relevant, sufficiently representative, and to the best extent possible free of errors and complete.

obligations.title: Technical Documentation
obligations.description: Draw up technical documentation of the high-risk AI system before that system is placed on the market or put into service.
obligations.guidance: Comprehensive documentation as per Annex IV. Must cover system architecture, data, training, validation, documentation.

obligations.title: Record-Keeping
obligations.description: High-risk AI systems shall technically allow for the automatic recording of events (logs) over the lifetime of the system. Logging capabilities shall enable a level of traceability appropriate to the intended purpose of the system, covering (a) situations that may result in the AI system presenting a risk within the meaning of Article 79(1) or that may lead to a substantial modification, (b) facilitation of post-market monitoring referred to in Article 72, and (c) monitoring of the operation of the high-risk AI system referred to in Article 26(5).
obligations.guidance: Ensure the system can automatically record events (logs) over its lifetime with traceability appropriate to the intended purpose. Logs must support risk situations under Article 79(1) or substantial modification, post-market monitoring under Article 72, and operational monitoring under Article 26(5). Article 19 sets a six-month minimum retention period for automatically generated logs for providers.

obligations.title: Transparency and Provision of Information to Deployers
obligations.description: Provide deployers with all necessary information to use the high-risk AI system in compliance with this Regulation.
obligations.guidance: Provide clear instructions for use, expected level of accuracy, limitations, any human oversight measures.

obligations.title: Human Oversight
obligations.description: Design and develop high-risk AI systems in such a way that they can be effectively overseen by natural persons during the period in which the AI system is in use.
obligations.guidance: Enable humans to detect automation bias, unexpected outputs, and intervene or interrupt the system.

obligations.title: Accuracy, Robustness and Cybersecurity
obligations.description: Design and develop high-risk AI systems in such a way that they achieve an appropriate level of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity.
obligations.guidance: Implement measures to ensure accuracy, resilience to errors, resistance to cyber-attacks, and reliable output.

obligations.title: Quality Management System
obligations.description: Establish, implement, document and maintain a quality management system to ensure and demonstrate conformity with this Regulation.
obligations.guidance: ISO 9001-compliant QMS covering design, development, testing, validation, documentation and maintenance.

obligations.title: Article 43: Conformity Assessment for High-Risk AI Systems
obligations.description: Article **43** determines **which conformity assessment procedure** a high-risk AI system must follow before it can be placed on the market or put into service. For **Annex III point 1** (biometric) systems where harmonised standards or common specifications have been applied, the provider may choose between **internal control** (Annex VI) or **notified body** assessment (Annex VII). Where harmonised standards do not exist, are not applied, or are published with restrictions, the **notified body** route (Annex VII) is mandatory for point 1 systems. For **Annex III points 2 to 8**, providers follow **internal control** (Annex VI) with no notified body involvement. For **Annex I** product-law systems, the existing sectoral conformity assessment procedure applies, integrating AI Act Section 2
obligations.guidance: Perform self-assessment or third-party assessment as per Annex V/VI/IX. Affix CE marking if compliant.

obligations.title: Post-Market Monitoring by Providers
obligations.description: Establish and document a post-market monitoring system to keep monitoring the compliance of AI systems with this Regulation.
obligations.guidance: Continuously monitor system performance, collect and analyze relevant data, report serious incidents to authorities.

obligations.title: EU Database Registration
obligations.description: Before placing on the market or putting into service a high-risk AI system, the provider shall register the system in the EU database referred to in Article 71.
obligations.guidance: Register the AI system in the EU public database before market placement. Include provider identity, system description, intended purpose, risk level, conformity assessment status, and Member States where the system is placed on the market.

obligations.title: Human Oversight
obligations.description: Ensure that natural persons effectively oversee the high-risk AI system during the period in which the AI system is in use.
obligations.guidance: Assign competent human personnel to monitor system operation and intervene when necessary.

obligations.title: Data Quality and Governance
obligations.description: Use high-risk AI systems in such a way that appropriate data governance and management practices are applied.
obligations.guidance: Ensure relevant, sufficiently representative, accurate and complete input data for the system.

obligations.title: Fundamental Rights Impact Assessment
obligations.description: Before deploying a high-risk AI system, carry out a fundamental rights impact assessment (FRIA) to evaluate the impact on the rights of persons affected.
obligations.guidance: Conduct a FRIA covering: description of deployer's processes using the AI system, period and frequency of use, categories of affected persons, specific risks of harm, human oversight measures, and measures taken in case of materialization of risks. Notify the relevant market surveillance authority of the results.

obligations.title: Provide Information to Affected Persons
obligations.description: Inform natural persons that they are subject to the use of the high-risk AI system, unless the deployer does not have access to the information.
obligations.guidance: Inform affected natural persons of the use of the high-risk AI system (Article 26(11)). Where individual decision-making is involved, also consider the right to explanation under Article 86.

obligations.title: Chatbot Disclosure
obligations.description: Ensure that users are informed that they are interacting with an AI system unless this is obvious from the circumstances and the context of use.
obligations.guidance: Display clear indication that the interaction is with an AI system. Ensure disclosure is visible and understandable.

obligations.title: Deepfake Disclosure
obligations.description: Label artificially generated or manipulated image, audio or video content as such.
obligations.guidance: Clearly mark AI-generated content. Include metadata where technically feasible. Exception for authorized law enforcement.

obligations.title: Emotion Recognition Disclosure
obligations.description: Inform natural persons that they are subject to emotion recognition systems unless this is obvious from the circumstances.
obligations.guidance: Notify individuals when emotion recognition is being used. Obtain consent where required by data protection law.

obligations.title: General Transparency Obligations
obligations.description: Comply with transparency obligations when deploying limited-risk AI systems subject to this Article.
obligations.guidance: Ensure AI system interactions are clearly identified. Provide adequate information to users about system capabilities and limitations.

obligations.title: Article 16: Obligations of Providers of High-Risk AI Systems
obligations.description: Article 16 is the master obligation list for providers of high-risk AI systems. It consolidates every duty a provider must fulfil before and after placing a high-risk system on the EU market or putting it into service. Rather than creating new rules, it acts as a routing table: each lettered point references a specific requirement article (Articles 8-15, 17, 43, 47-49, 72) so the provider can track every obligation in one place. Always verify on [EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=OJ:L_202401689#article-16).
obligations.guidance: Map every Article 16 lettered obligation (a), (j) to an internal workstream owner and timeline.

obligations.title: Article 18: Documentation Keeping
obligations.description: Article 18 requires providers of high-risk AI systems to keep specified documentation available for market surveillance authorities for a period of 10 years after the system has been placed on the market or put into service. The documentation includes: (a) the [technical documentation](/en/ai-act-guide/article-11-technical-documentation) (Annex IV); (b) the documentation on the [quality management system](/en/ai-act-guide/article-17); (c) any changes approved by notified bodies (where applicable); (d) the decisions and documents issued by notified bodies; (e) the [EU declaration of conformity](/en/ai-act-guide/article-47). Providers must also keep automatically generated logs within their control, to the extent such logs are generated by the system under [Article 12](/en/ai-act-guide/article-12).
obligations.guidance: Establish a 10-year document retention policy for all Article 18 categories.

obligations.title: Article 19: Automatically Generated Logs
obligations.description: Article 19 requires providers of high-risk AI systems to keep the automatically generated logs (as provided for in [Article 12](/en/ai-act-guide/article-12)) for a period appropriate to the intended purpose of the system, and at least 6 months unless otherwise provided by applicable Union or national law (including GDPR). This complements Article 18 (documentation keeping) by specifically addressing operational logs rather than static documentation. The provider must keep logs to the extent the logs are under their control.
obligations.guidance: Set log retention to at least 6 months, extend if the intended purpose requires longer.

obligations.title: Article 20: Corrective Actions and Duty of Information
obligations.description: Article 20 requires providers of high-risk AI systems to take immediate corrective action when they consider or have reason to consider that a system they placed on the market or put into service is not in conformity with the Regulation. The provider must bring the system into conformity, withdraw it, or recall it as appropriate. When the system presents a risk (within Article 79(1)), the provider must immediately inform the national competent authorities of the Member State(s) where the system is available, giving details of the non-conformity and corrective measures taken. This is the provider's proactive self-correction duty.
obligations.guidance: Establish internal escalation procedures to surface non-conformity immediately.

obligations.title: Article 21: Cooperation with Competent Authorities
obligations.description: Article 21 requires providers of high-risk AI systems, upon a reasoned request from a national competent authority, to provide all information and documentation necessary to demonstrate conformity with Chapter III, Section 2 requirements, in an official Union language determined by the requesting authority. Providers must also cooperate with authorities on any action taken in relation to the system. This is the general cooperation backbone that supports Article 74 market surveillance and Article 79 enforcement procedures.
obligations.guidance: Establish an authority request handling procedure with defined response timelines.

obligations.title: Article 22: Authorised Representatives of Providers of High-Risk AI Systems
obligations.description: Article 22 requires providers of high-risk AI systems established in third countries to appoint an authorised representative established in the Union by written mandate before placing the system on the market or making it available. The representative must be empowered to: (a) verify that the EU declaration of conformity and Annex IV technical documentation have been drawn up; (b) keep documentation available for authorities for 10 years; (c) cooperate with national competent authorities on corrective actions; (d) terminate the mandate if the provider acts contrary to its obligations. This is the high-risk AI system counterpart to [Article 54](/en/ai-act-guide/article-54) (GPAI models).
obligations.guidance: Determine if the high-risk AI system provider is established outside the Union.

obligations.title: Article 23: Obligations of Importers
obligations.description: Article 23 places gate-keeping obligations on importers of high-risk AI systems. Before placing a system on the Union market, importers must verify that: (a) the conformity assessment has been carried out; (b) the provider has drawn up the Annex IV technical documentation; (c) the system bears CE marking; (d) the system is accompanied by the EU declaration of conformity and instructions for use; (e) the provider has appointed an authorised representative where required ([Article 22](/en/ai-act-guide/article-22)). Importers must also indicate their name, trade name, and contact address on the system or packaging, and inform the provider and market surveillance authority if the system presents a risk.
obligations.guidance: Before import: verify conformity assessment, CE marking, EU declaration, instructions for use, and authorised representative.

obligations.title: Article 24: Obligations of Distributors
obligations.description: Article 24 places verification obligations on distributors of high-risk AI systems. Before making a system available on the market, distributors must verify that: the system bears the CE marking; it is accompanied by the EU declaration of conformity and instructions for use; and the provider and importer have complied with their respective obligations. Distributors must also ensure storage and transport conditions do not compromise compliance, and inform the provider or importer and market surveillance authority if the system presents a risk.
obligations.guidance: Before making available: verify CE marking, EU declaration, instructions for use.

obligations.title: Article 25: Responsibilities Along the AI Value Chain
obligations.description: Article 25 is the re-qualification trigger: it defines when a distributor, importer, deployer, or third party becomes a provider of a high-risk AI system and inherits the full provider obligations under [Article 16](/en/ai-act-guide/article-16). This happens when they: (a) put their name or trademark on a system already placed on the market; (b) make a substantial modification; or (c) modify the system's intended purpose so it becomes high-risk. The original provider is released from Article 16 duties once the new provider is properly identified. Critical for deployer due diligence, any modification beyond normal use may shift obligations.
obligations.guidance: Include Article 25 analysis in all change control and modification approval workflows.

obligations.title: Article 47: EU Declaration of Conformity
obligations.description: Article 47 requires providers of high-risk AI systems to draw up a written, machine-readable EU declaration of conformity for each system and keep it available for 10 years after market placement. The declaration must contain the information set out in [Annex V](/en/ai-act-guide/annex-v), be updated as necessary, and be translated into the language(s) required by the Member State(s) where the system is made available. For dual-regulated products under Annex I legislation, a single declaration may cover both the AI Act and the sectoral requirements.
obligations.guidance: Map Annex V content requirements into a declaration template.

obligations.title: Article 48: CE Marking for High-Risk AI Systems
obligations.description: Article 48 requires the CE marking to be affixed to high-risk AI systems to indicate conformity with the Regulation. The marking must be affixed visibly, legibly, and indelibly to the AI system or, where not possible, to its packaging or accompanying documentation. The CE marking is subject to the general principles in Regulation (EC) No 765/2008 (the NLF accreditation and market surveillance regulation). For AI systems that are purely digital (no physical product), the CE marking appears in the digital documentation or user interface.
obligations.guidance: Complete conformity assessment (Article 43) and issue EU declaration (Article 47) before affixing CE marking.

obligations.title: Article 53: Obligations for Providers of General-Purpose AI Models
obligations.description: Article 53 is the operational backbone of Chapter V: it sets the baseline obligations that every provider of a GPAI model must meet when placing the model on the Union market-regardless of systemic-risk status. The four pillars: (1)(a) prepare technical documentation per [Annex XI](/en/ai-act-guide/annex-xi); (1)(b) provide downstream AI system providers with information and documentation to understand capabilities and limitations and comply with their own obligations; (1)(c) establish a policy to comply with Union copyright law, including the text and data mining opt-out regime under Directive (EU) 2019/790; (1)(d) make publicly available a sufficiently detailed summary of training content using a template provided by the AI Office. Article 53(2) provides a narrow exception for free and open-source GPAI models that are not systemic risk.
obligations.guidance: Prepare Annex XI Section 1 documentation (architecture, parameters, data provenance, compute, energy) for every model release on the Union market.

obligations.title: Article 55: Obligations for Providers of GPAI Models with Systemic Risk
obligations.description: Article 55 adds four additional obligations on top of the [Article 53](/en/ai-act-guide/article-53) baseline for providers of GPAI models classified with systemic risk under [Article 51](/en/ai-act-guide/article-51): (a) perform model evaluation including adversarial testing; (b) assess and mitigate possible systemic risks; (c) track, document, and report serious incidents to the AI Office and national authorities; (d) ensure adequate cybersecurity protection. Compliance can be demonstrated through adherence to codes of practice under [Article 56](/en/ai-act-guide/article-56) or equivalent measures until harmonised standards are adopted.
obligations.guidance: Establish a model evaluation programme using standardised protocols (benchmarks, evaluations, stress tests) before each major release.

obligations.title: Article 73: Reporting of Serious Incidents
obligations.description: Article 73 requires providers of high-risk AI systems to report serious incidents to the market surveillance authorities of the Member State(s) where the incident occurred. Reports must be made immediately after the provider establishes a causal link (or reasonable likelihood) between the AI system and the incident, and no later than 15 days after becoming aware. For death or serious damage to health, an initial report must be submitted immediately and no later than 2 days after awareness. The article also covers follow-up reporting, deployer cooperation, and interaction with sectoral incident reporting. Always verify on [EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=OJ:L_202401689#article-73).
obligations.guidance: Define internal escalation procedures to surface potential serious incidents within hours, not days.

obligations.title: Article 86: Right to Lodge a Complaint with a Market Surveillance Authority
obligations.description: Article 86 grants any natural or legal person who has grounds to consider that there has been an infringement of the AI Act the right to lodge a complaint with the relevant market surveillance authority. The authority must handle complaints in accordance with national procedures, inform the complainant of progress and outcome within a reasonable time, and accept complaints from consumer organisations and other representative bodies. This provides a public enforcement mechanism paralleling the private explanation right in [Article 85](/en/ai-act-guide/article-85).
obligations.guidance: Identify which market surveillance authority in each Member State where you operate would receive complaints about your AI systems.
